prose.summary: Your aluminium window frames qualify for the reduced duty rate under the India-UAE CEPA because the product meets the rule of origin. This allows you to claim the preferential CEPA rate instead of the normal (MFN) rate, giving an estimated saving of 10000.00 AED on this shipment. Please review the claim checklist below to prepare the necessary documents.
prose.classification: The product is classified under tariff line 76101000, which covers doors, windows, and their frames and thresholds for doors of aluminium, with high confidence. You should confirm this tariff code with Indian customs or a customs broker before shipping.
prose.duty: Under the India-UAE CEPA, the normal (MFN) rate of 10% is reduced to a CEPA rate of 0%. Claiming this preferential rate yields an estimated duty saving of 10000.00 AED on your shipment value of 100000 AED.
prose.origin: The applicable rule of origin requires a change in tariff subheading (CTSH), meaning non-originating materials must be classified in a different 6-digit subheading than the final product, along with a value addition (VA) of at least 45% on an FOB basis (the price loaded on board at the UAE port). The product meets this rule because final manufacture took place in the UAE, the manufacturing goes beyond simple minimal operations, all 3 non-originating inputs met the tariff change requirement, and the build-down value addition reached 49.0% against the 45% threshold.

notes.text: The trade agreement does not specify whether the build-down and build-up calculation methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ from the estimate shown.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
The '+' in the rule CTSH + VA 45% is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
Inference: SWS is charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text found).
Inference: anti-dumping and safeguard duties still apply (no exemption found).
Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is seen only in secondary sources (CBIC Instruction 28/2022), not the official text.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
